\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{అదృశ్యం} (adṛśyaṁ)}{అదృశ్యం (adṛśyaṁ)}]{\te{అదృశ్యం} (adṛśyaṁ) — a disappearance; vanished}

\label{lesson:TE-C353-adrsyam}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for to turn in, then the Telugu for to step aside.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{అదృశ్యం}}
\textbf{\te{అదృశ్యం}} — \emph{adṛśyaṁ} — \textquotedblleft{}a disappearance; vanished\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\te{ఆ} \te{పాప} \te{అదృశ్యం} \te{అందరినీ} \te{భయపెట్టింది}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā pāpa adṛśyaṁ andarinī bhayapeṭṭindi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The child's disappearance frightened everyone.
\end{quote}

\te{అదృశ్యమైంది}, has gone missing: the news form.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{అదృశ్యం}} (\emph{adṛśyaṁ}) is borrowed from Sanskrit \emph{adṛśya}, \textquotedblleft{}invisible, latent\textquotedblright{} (Monier-Williams), from \emph{a-}, \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{dṛś}, \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adṛśyaṁ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{adṛśyaṁ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā pāpa adṛśyaṁ andarinī bhayapeṭṭindi.} — The child's disappearance frightened everyone.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for to turn in, then the Telugu for to step aside, then say \emph{adṛśyaṁ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{అదృశ్యం} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A disappearance; vanished\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{మాయమవు} (māyamavu)}{మాయమవు (māyamavu)}]{\te{మాయమవు} (māyamavu) — to vanish; to disappear}

\label{lesson:TE-C353-mayamavu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for to step aside, then the Telugu for a disappearance.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{మాయమవు}}
\textbf{\te{మాయమవు}} — \emph{māyamavu} — \textquotedblleft{}to vanish; to disappear\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\te{నా} \te{సైకిలు} \te{రాత్రికి} \te{రాత్రే} \te{మాయమైంది}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{nā saikilu rātriki rātrē māyamaindi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
My bicycle vanished overnight.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \te{మాయమయ్యాను}, \emph{māyamayyānu}.

\te{మాయం}, vanished, with \te{అవు}, to become.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{మాయమవు}} (\emph{māyamavu}) is built on Sanskrit \emph{māyā}, \textquotedblleft{}supernatural power; illusion\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 10060), with the Telugu verb \emph{avu}, \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}: to go as if by magic.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māyamavu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māyamavu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{nā saikilu rātriki rātrē māyamaindi.} — My bicycle vanished overnight.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for to step aside, then the Telugu for a disappearance, then say \emph{māyamavu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \te{మాయమవు} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To vanish; to disappear\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{కనుమరుగవు} (kanumarugavu)}{కనుమరుగవు (kanumarugavu)}]{\te{కనుమరుగవు} (kanumarugavu) — to fade from view}

\label{lesson:TE-C353-kanumarugavu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for a disappearance, then the Telugu for to vanish.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{కనుమరుగవు}}
\textbf{\te{కనుమరుగవు}} — \emph{kanumarugavu} — \textquotedblleft{}to fade from view\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\te{ఆ} \te{పాత} \te{ఆచారాలు} \te{క్రమంగా} \te{కనుమరుగయ్యాయి}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ā pāta ācārālu kramaṅgā kanumarugayyāyi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Those old customs gradually faded away.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \te{కనుమరుగయ్యాను}, \emph{kanumarugayyānu}.

\te{కను}, eye, \te{మరుగు}, hiding, and \te{అవు}: to go hidden from the eye.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{కనుమరుగవు}} (\emph{kanumarugavu}) is a native compound: \emph{kanu}, \textquotedblleft{}the eye\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1159), \emph{maṟugu}, \textquotedblleft{}to be concealed\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4760, beside \emph{maṟacu}, \textquotedblleft{}to forget\textquotedblright{}), and \emph{avu}, \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kanumarugavu}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kanumarugavu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ā pāta ācārālu kramaṅgā kanumarugayyāyi.} — Those old customs gradually faded away.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for a disappearance, then the Telugu for to vanish, then say \emph{kanumarugavu} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{ప్రత్యక్షమవు} (pratyakṣamavu)}{ప్రత్యక్షమవు (pratyakṣamavu)}]{\te{ప్రత్యక్షమవు} (pratyakṣamavu) — to appear suddenly}

\label{lesson:TE-C353-pratyaksamavu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for to vanish, then the Telugu for to fade from view.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{ప్రత్యక్షమవు}}
\textbf{\te{ప్రత్యక్షమవు}} — \emph{pratyakṣamavu} — \textquotedblleft{}to appear suddenly\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\te{మాయమైన} \te{కుక్క} \te{మరుసటి} \te{రోజు} \te{ప్రత్యక్షమైంది}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{māyamaina kukka marusaṭi rōju pratyakṣamaindi.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The dog that had vanished turned up the next day.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \te{ప్రత్యక్షమయ్యాను}, \emph{pratyakṣamayyānu}.

\te{ప్రత్యక్షం}, before the eyes, with \te{అవు}, to become.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{ప్రత్యక్షమవు}} (\emph{pratyakṣamavu}) is built on Sanskrit \emph{pratyakṣa}, \textquotedblleft{}before the eyes, visible\textquotedblright{} (CDIAL 8635), with the Telugu verb \emph{avu}, \textquotedblleft{}to become\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pratyakṣamavu}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māyamaina kukka marusaṭi rōju pratyakṣamaindi.} — The dog that had vanished turned up the next day.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for to vanish, then the Telugu for to fade from view, then say \emph{pratyakṣamavu} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\te{కనిపెట్టు} (kanipeṭṭu)}{కనిపెట్టు (kanipeṭṭu)}]{\te{కనిపెట్టు} (kanipeṭṭu) — to detect; to find out}

\label{lesson:TE-C353-kanipettu}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Telugu for to fade from view, then the Telugu for to appear suddenly.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \te{కనిపెట్టు}}
\textbf{\te{కనిపెట్టు}} — \emph{kanipeṭṭu} — \textquotedblleft{}to detect; to find out\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\te{పోలీసులు} \te{దొంగ} \te{ఇల్లు} \te{కనిపెట్టారు}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{pōlīsulu doṅga illu kanipeṭṭāru.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The police found out the thief's house.
\end{quote}

Past (I …): \te{కనిపెట్టాను}, \emph{kanipeṭṭānu}.

Also to invent: \te{ఆయన} \te{కొత్త} \te{యంత్రం} \te{కనిపెట్టాడు}, he invented a new machine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\te{కనిపెట్టు}} (\emph{kanipeṭṭu}) is a native compound: \emph{kanu}, \textquotedblleft{}to see\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 1443), and \emph{peṭṭu}, \textquotedblleft{}to put, place\textquotedblright{} (DEDR 4390).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Telugu for to fade from view, then the Telugu for to appear suddenly, then say \emph{kanipeṭṭu} again
\end{itemize}
